Prevention: Avoid growing pineapples in shade, humid areas and acidic soils in agroecological zone
Avoid planting on land that has previously grown pineapples.
Raise planting beds at least 23 cm high for settling of the plant.
Make trenches to be between raised beds, to get rid of excess water without causing soil erosion.
Plant the crop on well drained non- heavy soils, and not in low land.
Plant disease free planting materials with space of at least 60 cm.
During ridging, be carefully not to pour soil in the whorl of the pineapple suckers.
Before you plan to start pineapple growing, bring your soil samples for soil analysis to
If results indicate acidic soil, then you will be advised whether to use lime or grow other crops.
Always disinfect the tools used in the pineapple field prevent the spread of the disease.
Monitoring: Heart rot is a water mould disease that causes complete rotting of the middle leaves.
Leaves turn brown with the base having water-soaked lesions.
Infected leaves pull out so easily and have a foul smell.
Start scouting for symptoms 2 weeks after planting as this is the most susceptible stage.
Continue regular scouting even when you do not see infection.
Plants of all ages, base of the middle leaves.
Leaf tips and margins of heart leaves.
Pale green colour, sometimes curled heart leaves, or light brown yellowish necrotic leaf edges.
Before plants get symptoms, thus when few symptoms are seen in the field or nearby
When 25 to 50 % of the field is infected nothing can be done.
Direct Control: Uproot all diseased plants and put them into the bag and burn them outside the field.

FRAC M03 mixed in 10L of water .
